question: The rash of Henoch Schonlein Purpura (IgA vasculitis) is characteristically non-blanching and predominantly distributed over the lower limbs and buttocks.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Recall the pathophysiology: the purpura of HSP is non-blanching because it is caused by red blood cell extravasation through inflamed vessel walls, not vasodilatation. The lower-limb/buttock predominance is a hallmark feature used in diagnostic criteria.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The palpable, non-blanching purpura of HSP (IgA vasculitis) results from IgA1 immune complex deposition in small vessel walls causing leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Gravity-dependent distribution — lower limbs and buttocks — is characteristic.
